item.title: Madonna Remembers William Orbit With Emotional Tribute: ‘You Were My Ray of Light’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we're remembering a musical legend. Madonna is paying tribute to her longtime collaborator and friend, William Orbit, who passed away at the age of 69.
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: Madonna took to social media to share her memories of working with Orbit, who produced her iconic album "Ray of Light". She wrote, "I had an epiphany when I met you and started working with you. I realized that music didn't have to fit into categories or genres. So we created our own."
[Clip of Madonna's acceptance speech at the 1999 Grammy Awards plays]
Host: The two first worked together when Orbit remixed Madonna's songs "Justify My Love" and "Erotica", before collaborating on "Ray of Light" in 1998. Madonna credited Orbit with inspiring her to experiment with new sounds and styles, saying "You pressed a magic button inside of me and I fell into a galaxy of unrealized dreams."
[Soft music continues]
Host: Orbit's signature sound, which blended techno, trip-hop, and downtempo elements, was a key part of the album's success. Madonna also worked with Orbit on other projects, including "Beautiful Stranger", "American Pie", and her albums "Music" and "MDNA".
[Clip of Madonna's song "Drowned World" plays]
Host: In her tribute, Madonna remembered the magical time they spent together in the studio, saying "I miss those days. Only you could inspire me to write a song like Drowned World or Swim. You were so otherworldly. So singular."
[Soft music fades out]
Host: Madonna's full tribute to William Orbit can be found on her Instagram page. We're remembering a talented producer and collaborator who left an indelible mark on the music world. Rest in peace, William Orbit.
[Outro music plays]
